root_cause.text: The zero_vruntime tracking (via avg_vruntime) was only updated at tick boundaries and full enqueue/dequeue, but not during slice expiration in the context switch path (put_prev/set_next), allowing two yield-bound tasks to rapidly leapfrog and cause zero_vruntime to drift, potentially leading to overflow and system instability.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states: "All that moves zero_vruntime are tick and full {de,en}queue.", and "Therefore, just like with the yield() case, force an update at the end of every slice." The patch moves avg_vruntime() from entity_tick() to update_deadline() and calls update_deadline() in yield_task_fair() instead of directly modifying deadline.

candidates.rationale: This statement sets the deadline when a task's slice expires, but it does not update avg_vruntime (zero_vruntime). According to the root cause, avg_vruntime should be updated during slice expiration in the context switch path to prevent drift, but it was only updated at tick boundaries. This missing update allows yield-bound tasks to rapidly leapfrog and cause zero_vruntime drift.

This call in entity_tick was the only place avg_vruntime was updated at tick boundaries. It is insufficient because it does not cover slice expiration in the context switch path. The removal of this call (as part of the fix) indicates that the update is moved elsewhere, confirming that the prior reliance on this single update point was vulnerable.
